Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1) Proceed with in-person neurological assessment and dilated fundoscopic examination; obtain baseline vital signs (including blood pressure) as part of evaluation for new persistent headache; book appointment via support line; if symptoms settle, appointment may be canceled.
- 2) Initiate acute headache management: prescribe a stronger NSAID alternative to ibuprofen (name, dose, route, and frequency not documented) and continue acetaminophen as needed; instruct taking with food; reassess response and escalate if headache worsens or persists.
- 3) Evaluate potential migraine with aura given visual symptoms (photophobia, transient visual phenomena); review impact of symptoms on daily activities and sleep; plan to reassess after initial treatment with results of neurological exam and fundoscopy.
- 4) Review combined oral contraceptive pill in context of new migraine-like headaches; plan to perform blood pressure check to help determine pill suitability; discuss potential need to change the pill if migraine features persist or worsen.
- 5) Follow-up and safety: if headaches worsen, change in character, development of red flags, fever, neck stiffness, focal neurologic symptoms, go to emergency department; otherwise proceed with scheduled full examination; if symptoms resolve, appointment can be canceled.
- 6) Referral/specialist planning: if needed, arrange referral or further evaluation through the support team after the full examination.
- 7) Additional patient instructions: take prescribed medications with food; BP will be checked at the appointment to ensure ongoing suitability of contraceptive therapy.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: New, severe blinding headache for three days causing significant difficulty concentrating and inability to work.
- Onset, duration, progression: Sudden onset three days ago upon waking; persistent; fluctuates with brief improvement after ibuprofen but not resolved.
- Location and quality: Headache described as global with relative prominence around the right eye.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia/light sensitivity; occasional “shooting” visual phenomena; no nausea or vomiting reported.
- Eye/vision: Recent eye check with no changes in vision.
- Neurologic: No reported weakness, numbness, or changes in smell/taste.
- Sleep: Sleeping well; headache not waking from sleep; may awaken in the morning.
- Triggers/precipitants: Standing up quickly may cause brief stabbing pain; moving head may feel as if something is moving inside.
- Past medical history: History of episodic headaches in the past; one prior short episode resolved with ibuprofen; mother has migraines.
- Medications: Oral contraceptive pill (started ~1 year ago); intermittent ibuprofen for headaches; no other medications reported.
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Lives alone; non-smoker; alcohol use approx. 3 drinks per week.
- Review of systems: No fever; no nasal/sinus symptoms; no cough or phlegm; no weight change; energy described as low due to ongoing headaches.
- Red flags: No fever, no focal neurological symptoms reported.

Objective:
- No objective vital signs or physical examination findings documented in the transcript.
- Recent eye exam reported by patient with no vision changes; exam findings not provided.
- Plan includes neurological examination and dilated fundoscopic examination; blood pressure measurement planned.
- Areas noted to be assessed but not yet evaluated: fundus, neurological status, vitals.

Assessment & Plan:

1. New-onset persistent headache with photophobia and visual phenomena (likely migraine-type headache)
   - Assessment: Migraine-type headache is suspected; visual symptoms raise concern for migraine with aura; no red flags documented.
   - Differential diagnosis (if applicable): Migraine with aura; tension-type headache; secondary headache not ruled out without exam.
   - Investigations planned: In-person neurological examination; dilated fundoscopic examination; blood pressure measurement at visit.
   - Treatments planned: Prescription of a stronger NSAID alternative to ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) and concurrent acetaminophen; take analgesics with food.
   - Referrals: Full in-person examination arranged via support line; follow-up to reassess; appointment may be canceled if symptoms resolve.

2. Management of combined oral contraceptive pill in context of new migraine-like headaches
   - Assessment: Headache features with visual symptoms may impact pill suitability; BP check will inform decisions.
   - Investigations planned: Blood pressure measurement at the appointment to assess suitability of continued hormonal therapy.
   - Treatments planned: Continue current pill for now; consider changing the pill if migraine features persist or worsen (discussion to occur after full evaluation).
   - Referrals: No immediate specialty referral specified; pill management to be revisited at follow-up.

3. Safety and follow-up plan
   - Assessment: Monitor progression; escalate if symptoms worsen or new red flags develop.
   - Investigations planned: None beyond planned neurological exam, fundus, and BP at follow-up.
   - Treatments planned: Continue current analgesic plan; reassess after examination.
   - Referrals: If needed, arrange further specialist evaluation via the support team after full examination.

Quality checks (document quality and gaps):
- Missing elements clinically expected: No documented vital signs or full physical exam; exact medication names, doses, routes, and frequencies for the stronger NSAID are not documented; precise pill name and dosing for the contraceptive pill are not documented; no imaging or labs results available.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Generally comprehensible; occasional brief audio issues and incomplete details on specific medication names and dosing.

Notes:
- A COVID-19 vaccine suitability assessment was not mentioned in the transcript.
- All patient education and safety notes are to be provided during the in-person visit, including red-flag instructions and the plan to contact support for urgent concerns.
